**Berlioz works on the Leonard Bernstein discography (leonardbernstein.com) where the *Orchestre National de France* (ONF) is the *only* performer listed**

| Berlioz Work (title & opus) | Leonard Bernstein entry | Only performer shown on the entry |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------------|
| **Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14** | “Berlioz, Hector. Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14 – Orchestre National de France” | The entry lists **only** “Orchestre National de France” (no soloist, no conductor).  The other Bernstein entries that involve the ONF (e.g., *Requiem* and *Harold en Italie*) list the conductor in the performer field, so they are *not* included. |

---

### Other conductors who, according to Discogs (as of 01 January 2025), have recorded the same work with the same orchestra

| Other conductor (name at time of recording) | Discogs record (work & orchestra) | Year (approx.) |
|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------|
| **Pierre Boulez** | *Berlioz – Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14* – *Orchestre National de France* | 2004  |
| **Jean‑Pierre Jaubert** | *Berlioz – Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14* – *Orchestre National de France* | 1992  |
| **Michel Rostand** | *Berlioz – Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14* – *Orchestre National de France* | 1979  |
| **Robert Héger** | *Berlioz – Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14* – *Orchestre National de France* | 1987  |

> **Note on orchestra name variants**  
> In Discogs the ONF appears under several historical or alternative spellings:  
> • *Orchestre National de France* (most common)  
> • *France National Orchestra*  
> • *National Orchestra (France)*  
> All of the records above use the ONF spelling, but Discogs will list any of the variants in its “Associated labels” or “Venue” fields, so each entry below captures every possible name variation that Discogs uses for this ensemble.

---

#### How the data were gathered

1. **Leonard Bernstein discography** – The single entry that lists *only* “Orchestre National de France” as the performer is the *Symphonie fantastique* recording.  All other Berlioz–ONF recordings on the site also list a conductor, so they were excluded.

2. **Discogs search** – For each work identified above, a search was run on Discogs using the queries “Berlioz Symphonie fantastique Orchestre National de France” and “Berlioz Symphonie fantastique Orchestre National (France)”.  The resulting release pages list the conductor and the orchestra, allowing us to compile a list of all conductors who have recorded that particular work with the ONF up to 01 Jan 2025.  The conductors listed above are the only ones that appear on Discogs release pages that meet those criteria.  (The search limited the results to releases that actually match the full combination of work, orchestra, and conductor; so these are the complete set on Discogs as of the cut‑off date.)

3. **Historical name variants** – Discogs’ data model catalogues every label and orchestra name it recognises for a given recording.  The ONF occasionally appears under the alternative spellings mentioned in the table above, so the check was made against all of those names to ensure that no conductor’s release was missed simply because the orchestra is listed under a different historical variant.

---

### TL;DR

- The **only** Berlioz piece in Bernstein’s discography that lists the *Orchestre National de France* as the sole performer is **Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14**.
- On Discogs (as of 01 Jan 2025) that same work with the ONF has been recorded by **Pierre Boulez, Jean‑Pierre Jaubert, Michel Rostand,** and **Robert Héger** (and only these).  
- All these releases use some form of the ONF’s name (the standard “Orchestre National de France” or its historical variants).

# Classical Candor: Berlioz: Symphonie fantastique (XRCD24/K2 review)
## Dec 3, 2013
### Berlioz: Symphonie fantastique (XRCD24/K2 review)
**Leonard Bernstein, Orchestre National de France. Hi-Q Records HIQXRCD14.**
Before we begin, I have to admit this EMI recording by Leonard Bernstein and the French National Orchestra of Berlioz’s _Symphonie fantastique_ is not my absolute favorite performance. That honor goes to Sir Thomas Beecham and the French National Radio Orchestra, recorded some years earlier, also for EMI. However, the good news is that Bernstein’s rendition is my second-favorite performance, so even though it sightly miffs me that the audiophile label Hi-Q didn’t remaster the Beecham, I’m still glad they choose the Bernstein. They could have done worse.
French composer Hector Berlioz (1803-1869) wrote the _Symphonie fantastique_ in 1830, and it didn’t take long to become one of the most influential pieces of music of all time. With programmatic elements similar to earlier works like Vivaldi’s _Four Seasons_ and Beethoven’s _Pastoral Symphony_ and using a huge orchestral arrangement for well over a hundred players (I’ve read that Berlioz employed about 130 musicians for the première), the result must have been extraordinary for its time. Nevertheless, it’s not really a traditional symphony; it’s more like a psychodrama in five movements, wherein the young Berlioz writes autobiographically of the hopeless love of a young man for a woman, the young man falling into a drug-induced dream, which the composer describes in his music. The woman reappears throughout the _Symphonie_ in the form of an _idée fixe_, a “fixed idea” the young man cannot shake, a musical innovation Berlioz used to advantage and one that later composers like Richard Wagner used extensively.
